package.title: Why Soda Cans Explode at 30,000 Feet
package.description: Discover cabin pressure physics and why soda cans explode at high altitudes or deep underwater.
package.pinned_comment: Have you ever had a can pop open loudly on a plane? Tell us about your messy altitude experiences below!
key_facts: Airplane cabins are pressurized to a lower pressure than sea level, causing gas inside sealed containers to expand.
Deep-sea environments have extreme high pressure that has the opposite effect on sealed containers.
